nextStoryContext: US-003 landed `src/ui/TabBar.tsx`: a pure controlled presentational primitive, `TabBar({ tabs, activeIndex, onChange })` where `tabs: TabDef[]` is `{ label, confirmed?, value? }`. It owns NO internal index state -- unlike `Select.tsx` (local `useState` idx, `onChange` fires only on Enter), TabBar's own `useInput` computes the next index from the `activeIndex` PROP on every Left/Right press (wrap-around at the bounds: idx 0 + Left -> last idx, last idx + Right -> idx 0) and calls `onChange(next)` immediately -- the caller must hold the actual state and re-render with the new `activeIndex`. Each chip renders `[ label ]` (muted) or `[ label ]` bold+accent when `i === activeIndex`; a confirmed tab (`confirmed: true` AND `value !== undefined`) renders `[ label: value ]` instead of `[ label ]`. Colors come from `src/ui/theme.ts` (`colors.accent`/`colors.muted`), which re-exports `src/design/tokens.ts`'s `palette` -- no new tokens were added. Per the story notes and prior US-002 handoff, US-004 (`src/ui/ConfigScreen.tsx` refactor, ~568 lines today) is next: it must (a) replace the sequential forward-only wizard with TabBar-driven navigation across 7 tabs (6 phase tabs: Orchestrator/Planner/Auditor/Implementer/Reviewer/Ship, plus one Global tab folding backend/merge-mode/plan-approval/notify-recipient/notify-from -- the notify steps were added after the ConfigScreen issue was filed and must be preserved, not dropped), (b) reuse the existing per-phase model Select + custom-id passthrough (ConfigScreen.tsx:69-103, `PHASE_MODEL_OPTIONS`/`useCustomModelEntry`) rather than rebuilding it, (c) add the net-new effort Select (depends on US-001's `ConfigChoices.efforts`/`EFFORT_DEFAULTS`, still unwired into the live wizard per the US-002 handoff gap), and (d) extract per-tab sections to stay under biome's cognitive-complexity ceiling and the file-size budget (watch the keypress focus-advance logic in particular, a good extraction candidate). Test pattern for consuming TabBar from a stateful parent: see `test/ui/tab-bar.test.tsx`'s local `ControlledTabBar` wrapper (owns `useState`, threads `onChange` back into the `activeIndex` prop) -- ConfigScreen's own tests can drive tab switches with the SAME `stdin.write('\x1b[C')`/`stdin.write('\x1b[D')` shape once TabBar is wired in.
